title: Remediator SDK: lightweight guarded operator kit for safe, idempotent remediation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a small SDK and operator kit (Remediator) that converts high-frequency support runbook steps into executable, guarded tasks. Goals: make common remediation actions (rotate key, clear cache, restart shard, re-sync KV) callable from Console and CLI as idempotent, RBAC-gated operations with automatic telemetry and rollback hooks. This reduces oncall cognitive load and shortens time-to-remediate for recurring incidents.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Remediator SDK exposes a declarative action spec that includes preconditions, side-effect declarations, idempotency tokens, and rollback handlers.
A2: Console can render a task with parameters and a three-line safety summary; execution requires appropriate role and audit entry is generated.
A3: Execution path supports dry-run mode, automatic retries with backoff, and a visible operation trace in the Console timeline.
A4: Two sample actions implemented: cache-clear (memcached/redis) and service-restart (k8s deployment rolling restart) with unit and e2e tests.
A5: Integration test validates telemetry events (start/success/failure/rollback) flow to the operator-slo dashboard and alerts on >10% failure rate in 24h.
A6: Security review completed and KMS access for any credential use is through Customer KMS integration patterns.
A7: Documentation (Design doc + Console help + SDK quickstart) published with examples and Playbook mapping.
A8: No P0 incidents attributable to Remediator in the 2-week canary window on staging cluster.
implementation_plan: Step 1: Draft action DSL v1 (preconditions, inputs, outputs, side-effects, rollback) - design doc link.
Step 2: Implement SDK core (typescript + go bindings) and local runner for dry-run testing.
Step 3: Operator shim that schedules ephemeral pods with a scoped service account and enforces idempotency tokens.
Step 4: Console integration: interactive form + safety summary + audit log link.
Step 5: End-to-end tests against staging cluster; runbook-to-action mapping for top 8 recurring tasks.
Step 6: Security review and roles mapping; KMS/HSM integration follow-up if needed.
Step 7: Canary rollout to limited internal teams; gather SLIs and iterate.
Step 8: Publish docs, sample playbooks, and deprecate the ad-hoc shell scripts used by SRE.
technical_notes: Architecture: lightweight operator receives an Action CR (not persisted long-term) or a signed request from Console. Operator creates single-shot job pod with isolated SA, mounts only necessary secrets via projected KMS tokens, streams logs to the Console timeline, and emits structured telemetry (action.name, outcome, duration, idempotency_token, actor). Idempotency implemented with a job-leader-lock in the runtime namespace and optional external lockstore (redis) for cross-cluster cases. Rollback handlers are user-supplied commands invoked on failure. Safety: precondition evaluation runs in a read-only sandbox path with resource-limited sidecars to avoid cascading changes.
